canonicalExplanation.summary: A **CSS design system** is more than a list of colour and spacing variables. It's **tokens** (colour, spacing, type, radius), **components** built only from those tokens, a **layered** stylesheet structure, and proof that each component works in every **state** — default, hover, focus, error, disabled, long content, narrow container — plus documented **compatibility targets** and accessibility checks.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A team defines 40 colour and spacing variables and calls it a design system. Then the first long German button label overflows, the error state is missing, and a card breaks in the sidebar. Variables are the ingredients, not the meal. A small site reuses spacing and color tokens, while each component demonstrates default, focus, error, long-content and narrow states. In this lesson you'll deliver and explain a responsive, accessible and maintainable CSS system with documented compatibility targets.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know the **Responsive design and motion** module, **Stylesheet organization**, **Compatibility and progressive enhancement**, **Visual accessibility audit**, and **Semantic multi-page site** (the pages this system styles).

sections.heading: The model: tokens → layered components → proven states
Maintainable means predictable

includes: Build a token layer and layered components used across a small site.
Prove every component in all states, sizes and preferences, and document compatibility targets.

outcomes: Deliver and explain a responsive, accessible and maintainable CSS system with documented compatibility targets.

examples.title: Tokens plus components in every state
examples.situation: A small site reuses spacing and color tokens while each component demonstrates default, focus, error, long-content, and narrow states.
walkthrough: **Reuses tokens:** button, card, form field and nav use only spacing and colour tokens — a search finds no stray hex values.
**Each component demonstrates states:** the gallery page will render default, focus, error, long-content (German labels) and narrow (320px container) versions of each.
**Document:** the README lists the target matrix, audit results (zoom, keyboard, reduced motion, forced colours) and non-goals.
examples.result: The system is proven in every state and documented, so the team can build new pages confidently.

examples.title: The missing error state
examples.situation: A form field component has default and focus styles, but when validation fails, it looks identical — only the message text changes colour.
walkthrough: The state gallery shows the gap immediately.
Colour-only error text fails the audit.
Fix: an error state with a 2px `--color-error` border, an icon, and linked text; add it to the gallery.
examples.result: The error state is visible, accessible and part of the documented system.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: A design system is complete once colour and spacing variables are defined.
misconceptions.correction: Tokens are only the foundation. A system also needs components built from them, a predictable layer structure, every state proven in a gallery, accessibility audits, and documented compatibility targets.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The missing error state", what did the gallery reveal?

analogy.example: A design system is like a **LEGO set with instructions**: the bricks (tokens) matter, but the value is in the tested models (components) and the guide showing every configuration (state gallery, README).
usefulFor: states and docs complete the system
limitations: LEGO bricks don't change colour at night; your tokens should (dark mode).
Missing instruction pages are like undocumented states.

recap.summary: To deliver a responsive, accessible and maintainable CSS system, define a themed token layer, build layered components from tokens only, prove every state in a gallery, audit keyboard, zoom, motion and forced colours, and document compatibility targets and non-goals.
